title: Tucked in a Closet, Hidden by a Coat, a Lost Work by Georgia O’Keeffe
summary: A piece by the famed painter had been squirreled away for decades. Now it’s been found — and may sell for millions.

Several years ago, a woman was visiting her aunt in the East Village when the older woman casually mentioned that there was an O’Keeffe in the closet.


And yes, behind a Chanel suit and a velvet opera coat, in a box, sat a 10-inch-by-24-inch painting of tan, green and gray hills below a pale blue sky.


Georgia O’Keeffe, considered to be one of the most important artists in the 20th century, had made the piece in 1930. The aunt, who died this year at 90, had received it for a graduation gift from her mother, who purchased it for $3,800 in 1963, at the Downtown Gallery, O’Keeffe’s dealer in Manhattan.


The niece requested anonymity for the family, saying her aunt was a very private person who would not have been interested in drawing attention.


Over the past 63 years, the value of the painting, “Near Abiquiu, New Mexico I,” has grown considerably — to between $3 million and $5 million, according to Christie’s, which plans to auction the work on Tuesday.


The aunt had worked for the Foreign Service and was a world-ranked bridge master, her niece said Monday in an interview. The painting had hung in her East Village home for years — a bit out of place with other, significantly less valuable art, the niece said. Then, in the early 1980s, as O’Keeffe’s work soared in popularity and in value, a member of the aunt’s bridge club began paying an outsize interest in the work when the group would gather at her home.
